record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a set of points P in the plane.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let G be a finite simple graph given by its adjacency matrix. A finite set P of points in the Euclidean plane realizes G as its point visibility graph if there is a bijection between the vertices of G and the points of P such that two distinct points p, q ∈ P are adjacent in G if and only if the open line segment joining p and q contains no other point of P (equivalently, no third point of P lies on the segment between them). The decision problem is: given the adjacency matrix of G, determine whether such a finite point set P exists. Provide an algorithm that decides this problem, or characterize its computational complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has shown the recognition of point visibility graphs is NP-hard (Roy, 2014/2016) and, more strongly, complete for the existential theory of the reals ∃R (Cardinal & Hoffmann, SoCG 2015 / DCG 2017), which places it in PSPACE and hence makes it decidable. However, no efficient (polynomial-time) recognition algorithm is known, and an exact characterization of point visibility graphs remains open. Thus the problem is partially resolved: complexity-classified but no tractable algorithm or combinatorial characterization exists.

status_evidence.title: Point visibility graph recognition is NP-hard
status_evidence.snippet: A graph is constructed from a 3-SAT formula in polynomial time such that it is a point visibility graph iff the formula is satisfiable, proving NP-hardness.

status_evidence.title: Recognition and Complexity of Point Visibility Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The recognition problem for point visibility graphs is complete for the existential theory of the reals ∃R, hence in PSPACE.
status_evidence.claim: PVG recognition is ∃R-complete and therefore decidable but at least NP-hard.
